newsitem.title: UK: British-Borneo sees major drilling project.
newsitem.headline: British-Borneo sees major drilling project.

text.p: British-Borneo Petroleum Syndicate Plc, the UK oil exploration group, said on Thursday it would participate in around 30 exploration and appraisal wells this year, which it called its most ambitious drilling programme to date.

It planned to spend up to 75 million pounds($120.2 million) on the exploration and drilling programme and a further 100 million pounds on development projects, group chief executive Alan Gaynor said in the group's results statement.
Earlier, British-Borneo announced a jump in pretax profits to 19.51 million pounds in the year to December 31 from 13.63 million the previous year.
After-tax profits for the year were up by 38 percent to 14.4 million pounds, the company said.
The dividend per share rose 10 percent to a total 8.25 pence, while proven and probable booked reserves increased by 145 percent in 1996.
The company had a successful appraisal of the Morpeth field in the deep water Gulf of Mexico, with development now underway, and three further discoveries are under appraisal.

"1996 was a milestone year in our development as an operating oil company. We have created a substantial portfolio of opportunities to continue adding shareholder value both on the UK Continental Shelf and in the Gulf of Mexico, where our growth in the deep water area is just beginning," said Gaynor. ($ = 0.624 British Pounds)
